params_note: dense model; total includes the SigLIP vision tower + projector (0.423 B), text decoder + embeddings = 27.009 B
dtype_note: bf16 only; fp16 overflows in Gemma-3 and the adapter refuses it
weights_gb_note: decimal GB; bf16 = sum of safetensors sizes on the hub (equals 2 x params); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate: 26.009 B quantisable linear params x 0.5159 B + remaining params in bf16
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: yes (54.86 GB weights; core.batches() sizes batches from free memory); 4bit also possible (~16.3 GB) via adapter.load(quant='4bit') but not needed. CAVEAT (arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU): the weights and generation fit, but direction building is borderline on one 80 GB card. core.Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats (SPEC v1: model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True) keeps 63 full-sequence hidden states, all-position logits and a KV cache) forward chunks of up to 14,000 padded prompt tokens (core.batches tok_budget) and need 54.86 + 9.48 + 7.34 = 71.7 GB before the KV cache (up to 7.1 GB) and activations, i.e. 71.7-78.8 GB against ~85 GB on the card and the 76.5 GB (90%) line of the verdict rule in hidden_last_long_context. The single longest prompt of sbx.evals.get_pool()['hard'] (labbench/SeqQA, 2,144 tokens with framing E; the next longest has 1,493) needs only 57.4-58.5 GB. See hidden_last_long_context and known_issues.

hidden_last_long_context.assumes: core.Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats as of SPEC v1: one forward with output_hidden_states=True over a chunk of n prompts (left-padded to T tokens, the longest of the chunk) keeps (num_layers + 1) bf16 hidden states [n, T, hidden] and all-position logits [n, T, vocab], plus a KV cache (use_cache defaults to True; gb_kv_cache_upper_bound assumes full attention in every layer: exact for Llama, an over-estimate for Gemma's 5:1 sliding-window layers); the gb_* figures of the longest prompt are the n = 1 case; transient activations and allocator overhead are NOT counted, so the real need is higher
hidden_last_long_context.prompt_set: sbx.evals.get_pool()['hard'] (281 questions after the sbx.evals prompt-length cap MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500, 296 before it; sbx/dirs/sandbag.py:sandbag_hard calls ctx.hidden_last on all of them), framing E, google/gemma-3-4b-it tokenizer (same vocab as 12b / 27b)
hidden_last_long_context.verdict_rule: fits_80gb = gb_peak_upper_bound <= 0.9 * 85 (an '80 GB' A100/H100 has ~85e9 bytes; 10% headroom, the same rule as for the weights); a 'false' verdict additionally needs gb_peak_lower_bound > 0.9 * 85, i.e. it does not depend on the KV-cache term. Arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU

largest_chunk.basis: Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats forward chunks of prompts, not single prompts: core.batches() packs the prompts, shortest first, into chunks of at most tok_budget = 14000 padded prompt tokens (prompts x the longest prompt of the chunk; only a single prompt above the budget makes a bigger chunk) and that budget does not depend on the model or on the free memory, so the memory peak is set by the biggest chunk. The figures for the longest prompt alone underestimate it whenever that prompt is shorter than the budget, which holds for every pooled prompt since the sbx.evals prompt cap. tokens = max(tok_budget, longest_prompt_tokens) is an upper bound on the padded tokens of one chunk (a smaller prefill or KV budget on a small GPU can make the real chunks smaller); the sizes are the same formulas as above at that many tokens
largest_chunk.verdict_rule: fits = gb_peak_upper_bound <= 0.9 * 85; does not fit = gb_peak_lower_bound > 0.9 * 85 (independent of the KV-cache term); borderline = in between (the lower bound is below the 90% line, the upper bound is above it). Same thresholds as fits_80gb above. Arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (200/302 = accessible, 403 = gated and access not granted)

min_transformers_note: conservative: Gemma-3 itself exists since 4.50.0 (checkpoint config says 4.50.0.dev0), but the AutoModelForCausalLM -> Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration mapping, the checkpoint key conversion and the model.model.language_model layer layout were only verified on 4.57.6 (they date from the 4.52 VLM refactor as far as I know); adapter.layers() also resolves the 4.50-4.51 layout but that branch is stub-tested only

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(real hub config) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device) + tie_weights(); numerics of the 1-based convention on a tiny random model of the same HF class (sbx/tests/test_adapters_gemma_llama.py)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)

auto_class: AutoModelForCausalLM -> Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration in transformers 4.57.6 (verified; same class as AutoModelForImageTextToText); text-only use = pass input_ids only, the vision tower stays idle. All checkpoint keys map 1:1 through _checkpoint_conversion_mapping (only the tied lm_head.weight is absent from the checkpoint).

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured mean over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option questions) with the real tokenizer + adapter.build; the long-context sets are longer but bounded by the sbx.evals prompt-length cap (MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500): every question served by sbx.evals builds a framing-E prompt of at most 2,474 tokens (a GPQA-bio question) and the LAB-Bench sets average ~0.6k (labbench_seqqa), ~1.3k (labbench_protocolqa) and ~1.4k (labbench_cloning, 6 questions left) tokens with framing N; the raw LAB-Bench files have prompts of up to 51k characters (docs/evals.md section 3)

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ under the cot prompt (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run; max_new=512 truncates longer answers (they count as unparsed).
known_issues: Multimodal checkpoint: loads as Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration; the vision tower + projector (~0.42 B params, 0.85 GB bf16) are loaded but idle for text-only prompts.
bf16 only: fp16 overflows in Gemma-3 (the adapter's load() raises on fp16).

No system role: framings E/C/... are delivered as a prefix of the user turn (not a system prompt), unlike Llama (system) and gpt-oss (developer); keep this in mind when comparing framing effects across families.

Expected to be verbose (UNMEASURED, from prior knowledge of the model): a 'brief' step-by-step answer may run 200-400 tokens and 10-option sets could exceed max_new=512; truncated answers have no 'Answer: X' line and count as unparsed. Watch parse_rate on the first GPU run (raise max_new via ctx.run(max_new=...)).
Sliding-window attention (window 1024, 5 local : 1 global layer): for prompts > 1024 tokens (labbench_protocolqa / labbench_cloning) 5 of 6 layers only see the last 1024 tokens, as in training.

Shipped generation_config has do_sample=True, top_k=64, top_p=0.95 and cache_implementation='hybrid'; core passes do_sample=False (greedy), so HF prints a harmless 'generation flags are not valid' warning.
core.kv_bytes_per_token assumes full attention in every layer, so it over-estimates Gemma's KV cache (conservative: smaller batches).
Not run on real weights (none available locally): max_new, est_tokens_per_question and output formats are unmeasured; mechanics were verified on tiny random models of the same HF classes.
If load() is bypassed on transformers 4.50-4.51 the layer path differs (model.language_model.model.layers); adapter.layers() resolves it, but that branch is stub-tested only.

OOM risk for direction building on ONE 80 GB GPU (borderline; arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU; details in hidden_last_long_context): core.Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats (SPEC v1) run model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True), which keeps 63 full-sequence hidden states, all-position logits and a KV cache for a whole chunk of prompts, and core.batches() fills a chunk up to 14,000 padded prompt tokens (a fixed budget, independent of the hidden-state and logits memory of the model). For this key that is 54.9 + 9.5 + 7.3 = 71.7 GB before the KV cache (up to 7.1 GB) and activations, 71.7-78.8 GB in all, against ~85 GB on the card and the 76.5 GB (90%) line the verdict rule keeps free for activations and allocator overhead; the longest single prompt of sbx.evals.get_pool()['hard'] (labbench/SeqQA, 2,144 tokens with framing E) needs only 57.4-58.5 GB. hidden_last has no OOM fallback, so an out-of-memory error aborts the recipe that called it (sandbag_hard in sbx/dirs/sandbag.py) and loses the generation pass that ran before it (_collect_one writes its cache only after hidden_last). A core fix (capture only the last-token residual with forward hooks, pass use_cache=False and logits_to_keep=1) or a GPU with ~96 GB or more (e.g. a 141 GB H200) removes the risk. The pool is bounded by the sbx.evals prompt cap (MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500); a prompt above 14,000 tokens would form a chunk of its own with that many tokens. Until then fits_single_80gb is true for the weights and for generation only.
recommended_gpu: 1 x 80 GB (A100-80GB / H100) in bf16: 54.9 GB weights, ~20 GB left for KV cache and activations (enough for generation); hidden-state extraction (core.Ctx.hidden_last) is borderline on one 80 GB card with the current core: ~57-59 GB for the longest pooled prompt (2,144 tokens) but ~72-79 GB for the largest chunk core.batches() builds (14,000 padded prompt tokens), see hidden_last_long_context: it is safe only with a core fix or a GPU with ~96 GB or more (H200 141 GB); a 48 GB card needs quant='4bit' (~16.3 GB) for the weights alone.
download_gb_note: sum of the bf16 safetensors shards (plus a few MB of tokenizer/config files)

special_tokens.note: core pads finished rows with pad_token_id or eos_token_id = 1 (<eos>) because the pad id 0 is falsy; split() cuts at the first <end_of_turn>/<eos>
